context_requirements: Functional NR1H4 (FXR) expression; FXR is highest in liver, intestine, kidney, and adrenal, low in most other lineages
Presence of an FXR ligand-binding competent receptor; some lines may express low or dominant-negative FXR isoforms
For the antiproliferative/IL-6-STAT3 effects, an autocrine or paracrine IL-6/STAT3-driven context (e.g., HCC, colorectal)
For bile-acid and lipid target gene changes, an intact bile-acid/FXR transcriptional axis; hepatocyte-like or enterocyte-like phenotype
falsifiers: No change in canonical FXR target genes (NR0B2/SHP, ABCB11, SLC51A, SLC51B, ABCB4) at 24 h in any line, especially HEPG2 or HT29
No repression of CYP7A1 or other bile-acid synthesis genes in a line with intact FXR signaling
No reduction in IL-6/STAT3 target genes in HCC or colorectal lines despite FXR expression
Transcriptional changes indistinguishable from vehicle across all nine lines at both 6 h and 24 h
Changes that are reversed by an FXR antagonist (e.g., guggulsterone) would support the hypothesis; absence of such reversal in a responsive line would weaken it

evidence.supports: OCA regulates canonical FXR targets NR0B2, ABCB11, SLC51A, SLC51B, ABCB4 in human liver slices at 24 h
OCA causes cell cycle arrest and suppresses IL-6/STAT3 signaling with SOCS3 upregulation in HCC lines
GW4064 reduces lipogenic gene expression and hepatic steatosis in mice
GW4064 represses proinflammatory genes including IL-6, IL-1β, IFN-γ, MCP-1 in macrophages
6ECDCA reduces hepatic steatosis and oxidative stress in mice
